item.title: Capital flows, exchange rates and financial conditions in EMEs in an evolving international monetary system
item.description: The papers in this volume reflect the key themes discussed at the meeting, exploring the intersection of global and domestic factors shaping EMEs' financial conditions. They examine the evolving dynamics of capital flows and exchange rates, the role of local and foreign investors and the transmission of global financial shocks to EMEs.

item.title: Can the Climate Crisis Unite Europe?
item.description: The foundations of Europe’s postwar peace and prosperity are beginning to fracture, yet the European Union still struggles to unite its increasingly divided member states around a common political project. The escalating climate crisis could provide the continent with the shared purpose it has long lacked.

item.title: U.S. Sends Rare SPR Oil Cargo to Asia as Hormuz Crisis Reshapes Trade
item.description: A tanker loaded with crude oil from the U.S. strategic petroleum reserve has set off from the Gulf of Mexico to the Philippines in what is the first U.S. oil shipment to Asia since late 2022, Reuters reported, citing shipping data. The rare move yet again highlights the rearrangement of energy flows resulting from the shutdown of normal tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran and the United States. item.title: India Turns to Russia, Brazil, and Venezuela for Crude
item.description: The world’s third-largest crude importer, India, is accelerating efforts to diversify its oil imports in the wake of the Middle East crisis. India had begun raising imports from Russia three years before the Iran war cut off most supplies from the Middle East, on which India relies for about half of its crude purchases. With the Strait of Hormuz de facto closed and only a handful of tankers moving out of the chokepoint per week, and few of these India-bound, the country is looking further away for sources of crude.
